items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: the chaperones all met with Sid and Ellie ... Wertimer sometime on Friday before the party started

ctx.x: And how were the fraternities different back then.

Well we were a lot freer in our activities, although the college really didn’t like some of the partying that went on. Although at house party time a lot was forgiven. You know I mean the ladies, the dates were housed in the fraternity houses and all the guys had to move out and bunk in the dorms someplace. And so that was an interesting aspect to it. Another interesting aspect was the fact that every house, having a house party with dates in it, had to have a chaperone couple. And the chaperones all met with Sid…

Wertimer sometime on Friday before the party started, and rules were laid down. And it was pretty much controlled I would say. We had beer available in the house, we had a refrigerator downstairs, so there wasn’t a taboo on that at all. Some of the fraternities were a little wilder than others, depending upon the make-up of the people in it. And in our particular house we had all kinds of people. We had the athletes, we had the scholars, a Rhodes Scholar in one case, musicians, concert guys, you know the choir.…
